top_news.title: Astral Aviation, Zeal Global launch 767F twice-weekly Navi Mumbai-Nairobi freighter service for India-Africa cargo
top_news.summary: Astral Aviation, Africa's leading independent all-cargo airline, in partnership with Zeal Global Corp, a company listed on India's National Stock Exchange (NSE), is pleased to announce the launch of twice-weekly scheduled freighter services from Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMI) to its hub at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) in Nairobi, Kenya, with onward connections to Johannesburg, Juba, Mogadishu, Asmara, Port Sudan, Mwanza, Kigali and more than 50 destinations across the African continent. The new service will be operated using Astral Aviation's Boeing 767 freighter, providing dedicated cargo capacity between India's rapidly expanding commercial and manufacturing markets and Africa's emerging economies. Astral Aviation has partnered with Zeal Global for the new service, leveraging the company's expertise in air cargo sales, market development and freight forwarding relationships across India. Bridging the India-Africa Air Cargo Connectivity Gap India and Africa share long-standing economic, commercial and cultural ties, with bilateral trade spanning pharmaceuticals, healthcare products, engineering goods, automotive components, textiles, agricultural commodities and consumer products. Despite the growing importance of this trade corridor, dedicated freighter connectivity between India and many African markets remains limited, with cargo frequently routed through third-country hubs, resulting in additional transit times, handling costs and supply chain complexities. Astral Aviation's new Navi Mumbai-Nairobi service aims to address this connectivity gap by establishing a dedicated air cargo bridge between India and Africa, supported by Astral's extensive intra-African freighter network and strategic partnerships. articles.summary: Astral Aviation, Africa's leading independent all-cargo airline, in partnership with Zeal Global Corp, a company listed on India's National Stock Exchange (NSE), is pleased to announce the launch of twice-weekly scheduled freighter services from Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMI) to its hub at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) in Nairobi, Kenya, with onward connections to Johannesburg, Juba, Mogadishu, Asmara, Port Sudan, Mwanza, Kigali and more than 50 destinations across the African continent. The new service will be operated using Astral Aviation's Boeing 767 freighter, providing dedicated cargo capacity between India's rapidly expanding commercial and manufacturing markets and Africa's emerging economies. Astral Aviation has partnered with Zeal Global for the new service, leveraging the company's expertise in air cargo sales, market development and freight forwarding relationships across India. Bridging the India-Africa Air Cargo Connectivity Gap India and Africa share long-standing economic, commercial and cultural ties, with bilateral trade spanning pharmaceuticals, healthcare products, engineering goods, automotive components, textiles, agricultural commodities and consumer products. Despite the growing importance of this trade corridor, dedicated freighter connectivity between India and many African markets remains limited, with cargo frequently routed through third-country hubs, resulting in additional transit times, handling costs and supply chain complexities. Astral Aviation's new Navi Mumbai-Nairobi service aims to address this connectivity gap by establishing a dedicated air cargo bridge between India and Africa, supported by Astral's extensive intra-African freighter network and strategic partnerships.
